The call site additionally moved write=solo -> write=learn, which is the vocabulary every other read-only protection in this body uses (_ground_update, _explore_swap, _spawn_check, the halt EMA), so a grad-enabled instrument that forgot its no_grad is refused the cache too. So the callers that matter are the ways into FAB.forward, and all six were run: training+grad, eval+no_grad, eval+GRAD ON, leave-one-out+no_grad, leave-one-out+training=True+grad, and training+no_grad. Exactly ONE of the six writes the cache -- the gradient-carrying learning pass -- and the tensor it writes has a grad_fn. 0 of 6 leave a graphless tensor behind. A SEVENTH case, a direct `_identities(..., write=True)` under torch.no_grad(), leaves pop.ident_graph, pop.ident, pop.ident_step and pop.ident_live all identically unchanged -- which is the class claim tested rather than asserted.

findings.symbol: src/fabric/api.py::forward (FabricOut.aux_loss on the FAB_ON=0 and FAB_NORM_ONLY=1 arms)
findings.detail: CONFIRMED AND FIXED IN THE CODE, NOT IN THE RECORD. FabricOut's docstring requires '`aux_loss` is ONE scalar with a graph -- never a float and never a freshly allocated zero', and names `h.new_zeros(())` as what C2 cost; both early-return arms returned exactly that as their WHOLE aux_loss. It matters because the composition root SUMS this field into the objective it backwards (spine/compose.py's OPT.scaled_backward row: 'LM.lm_loss's mean + LM.anchor_term's already-weighted term + FabricOut.aux_loss + WORLD's loss'), so a graphless summand is an error at neither end -- backward() walks past it and the run reports normally. FIX: one line, `zero = h[:0].sum()` in place of `zero = h.new_zeros(())`. The sum of NO elements is exactly 0.0 for every h, carries h's graph, and its gradient is identically zero. I chose it over `h.sum() * 0.0`, which is nan whenever h is non-finite and would make FAB the apparent source of the LM's blow-up: measured, at FAB_ON=0 with an all-inf h, aux_loss is 0.0 and finite. I did NOT return None -- the root adds this into a sum, so None would turn switching the fabric off into a TypeError in the loop -- and I did NOT amend the frozen record docstring to carve out the two arms, because the task is to satisfy the requirement, not to weaken it. The terms are still ABSENT rather than zero on those arms and their gates still say so; only the record's guarantee changed from false to true. The same line also seeds the routed arm's depth_acc/bal_acc/aux, so aux carries a graph there even in the (unreachable at the defaults) case where every weighted term is off.
findings.repro: `python3 .../fab/item2.py` AFTER: FAB_ON=0 -> {value 0.0, has_graph TRUE, finite true, backward_ok true, dh_max 0.0}; FAB_NORM_ONLY=1 -> the same; shipped (routed) -> {value 0.5057754516601562, has_graph true} unchanged; 'FAB_ON=0 with inf h' -> {value 0.0, finite true, has_graph true}. BEFORE, the same script on git HEAD's file gives has_graph FALSE on the two off arms. NEIGHBOUR: the 30-step end-to-end A/B against HEAD at FAB_ON=0 and at FAB_NORM_ONLY=1 is EQUAL on every field -- the value was and is exactly 0.0, so nothing numerical moved; only the grad_fn did.

findings.symbol: src/fabric/api.py::forward (two training forward+backward calls at one step_windows)
findings.detail: REPRODUCED, RULED A CALLER ERROR, AND REFUSED BY NAME. Reproduced first: two forward+backward calls at step_windows=6 raise torch's 'Trying to backward through the graph a second time' at FAB_EMB_EVERY=1 AND at FAB_EMB_EVERY=4 -- and NOT at FAB_ROUTE_LEARN=0, which localises the cause to _identities' same-window branch handing the second pass the first pass's spent graph. THE RULING, FROM THE TREE'S OWN CLOCK RATHER THAN FROM TASTE. train/api.py::RunClock.advance is 'Advance one window. Returns Tick(step, epoch, flush_due, rolled, finished)' and the caller runs the flush body when flush_due; spine/compose.py's band B is the PER-FLUSH band (its own header: 'two stage letters, A (per window) and B (per flush)') and its FAB.forward row passes `step_windows=clock.step`; accumulation is spelled as more BACKWARDS over more WINDOWS (opt/api.py::scaled_backward counts Backwards and scales by accum; spine/derive.py::opt_steps_from_windows: 'effective_batch_windows is batch_windows x accum: windows per FLUSH times flushes per optimizer STEP'). So one window index is one routed training pass, and a caller that backwards twice at one index is mis-stating the clock. It is NOT a cache to be rebuilt: rebuilding would silently bless a second pass that applies this window's ponder anneal, balance anneal, spawn test, centroid EMA and halt EMA a second time. THE FIX: a new re-earned Population slot `learn_window`, and FAB.forward raises ValueError when a second gradient-carrying LEARNING pass arrives at the same step_windows. The message names step_windows and its value, the clock and the entry point that advances it, the torch error it replaces, the levers that spell accumulation, and the two things it does NOT refuse. THE REFUSAL IS ON THE CLOCK, NOT ON THE CACHE, ON PURPOSE: scoping it to the situation that actually raises would make it fire at FAB_ROUTE_LEARN=1 and vanish at FAB_ROUTE_LEARN=0, where the identical caller error currently raises NOTHING and doubles the window-keyed state in silence -- a guard that exists at one lever value and not another is the shape this package's own history is made of. Cost, stated rather than hidden: a caller that ran two grad-carrying training passes at one window index and got away with it at FAB_ROUTE_LEARN=0 now gets an exception; no caller in this tree does that (spine/compose.py's FAB.forward row is deferred and FAB.contribution, the one in-tree repeat-caller, is documented as no_grad and is still a stub).
findings.repro: BEFORE: `python3 .../fab/item3.py '{}'`, `... '{"FAB_EMB_EVERY":"4"}'` -> "RuntimeError: Trying to backward through the graph a second time..."; `... '{"FAB_ROUTE_LEARN":"0"}'` -> 'NO ERROR'. AFTER, all three -> "ValueError: FAB.forward: a SECOND gradient-carrying training pass at step_windows=6. The window clock advances once per window (train/api.py::RunClock.advance) ... An eval pass (training=False) or a leave-one-out pass (hold_out=...) at this window is legal and is not what this refuses." NEIGHBOURS IN THE SAME SCRIPT, both 'ok' before and after: two training passes at CONSECUTIVE windows (7 then 8), and eval(no_grad) -> leave-one-out(no_grad) -> training all at window 9. Plus the 15-config x 30-step A/B against HEAD, which runs one training pass per window for 30 windows and is EQUAL on every field including OPT_ACCUM=4.
